rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The primate album sorts into grades. New world monkeys — spider, howler, marmoset — live in the Americas with flat sideways nostrils and, uniquely, prehensile tails. Old world monkeys — macaque, langur, baboon — have downward nostrils, opposable thumbs, cheek pouches and sitting pads, but never grasping tails.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
New World: sideways nostrils + 2.1.3.3 + tail often prehensile.
Old World monkey: downward nostrils + 2.1.2.3 + tail not prehensile + ischial callosities.
Ape: no tail + long arms. Human: no tail + bipedal skeleton.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Prehensile vs non-prehensile tail:** prehensile tails grasp branches (new world spiders/howlers); old world tails only balance.  ·  **Monkey vs ape:** the surest single test is the tail — monkeys have one, apes do not.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Dental formulas are written incisors.canines.premolars.molars for one side of one jaw.  ·  Ischial callosities are sitting pads on the rump, not cheek pouches. Do not swap those two.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Spider monkey*** — new world prehensile-tail specialist.  ·  ***Rhesus macaque*** — old world monkey; the classical lab primate.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Learn the comparison as a 4-row table — distribution, nose, tail, thumb — enough for any 2–3m version.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Build the four-column comparison table.  ·  Sort four named animals using tail, then nose, then teeth.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "New = flat nose + grabbing tail; Old = down nose + sitting pads."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Q.** Name the four great apes. **Answer.** **Orangutan** (Asia), **gorilla** (Africa), **chimpanzee** (Africa) and **bonobo** (Africa) — all family Hominidae, our closest living relatives. The gibbon is a **lesser** ape, not a great ape.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: new vs old world monkeys; apes vs man.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The tail test and the thumb test:** tail separates monkey from ape; the opposable thumb and bipedal gait separate ape from man.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: New world (platyrrhine): S. America, flat side nostrils, prehensile tail, less opposable thumb, no cheek pouches — spider, howler, marmoset.  ·  Old world (catarrhine): Africa/Asia, downward nostrils, non-prehensile tail, opposable thumb, cheek pouches, ischial callosities — macaque, langur, baboon.  ·  Apes: tailless, arms > legs, knuckle-walk, 400–500 cc — gibbon (lesser), orangutan, gorilla, chimp (great).  ·  Man: bipedal, legs > arms, ~1400 cc, speech, chin, culture.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Old world monkeys and apes share the catarrhine nose — humans inherited it too.

rows.text: New World monkeys are recognised by → B  ·  Cheek pouches are typical of → B
